newsitem.title: CHINA: China, Malaysia set pulp venture study.
newsitem.headline: China, Malaysia set pulp venture study.

text.p: China and Malaysia signed a preliminary agreement to conduct a feasibility study for a possible joint venture pulp mill in Sarawak, Malaysian officials said on Monday.
They also said that a paper mill would be studied though they did not give the value of either project.
Primary Industries Minister Lim Keng Yaik told reporters that the pulp mill would have initial output of 500,000 tonnes annually and eventually that would rise to one million tonnes.
"We have identified the land," he told reporters.
He said that a Malaysian partner for the project had been chosen though he could not identify the company or say when the mill might be built.
Other officials said the pulp mill would be partly to supply the Malaysian market and partly for export.
Lim and other Malaysian officials are in China as part of a trade delegation led by Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad.
